newsitem.title: ITALY: VOLLEYBALL-VELASCO STEPS DOWN AS ITALY COACH.
newsitem.headline: VOLLEYBALL-VELASCO STEPS DOWN AS ITALY COACH.

text.p: Argentine Julio Velasco, the coach who took Italian men's volleyball to the world heights, announced on Tuesday that he was stepping down.

Velasco, whose standing in Italy is so great that he was even linked by some newspapers earlier this year to the job of coach of AC Milan soccer club despite having no football expertise, said he had not decided what to do next.
His resignation sent further ripples through Italian sport only a day after the departure of national soccer coach Arrigo Sacchi, who also happens to be a friend of his.

Unlike Sacchi, Velasco achieved almost everything at national level. In the year after he took charge in May 1989, he coached Italy team to the European crown, a silver medal in the World Cup, the World League title and Goodwill Games gold.
Under him, Italy won two world titles -- in 1993 and 1994 -- three European titles and five World Leagues.
